hook.text: Women have two X chromosomes but only use one per cell. The other is silenced into a clump called a Barr body.

buildup.text: Without X-inactivation, female cells would produce double the X-linked proteins. The imbalance would be lethal.

discovery.text: A gene called XIST coats one X chromosome in RNA, triggering methylation and histone changes that shut down the whole chromosome.

twist.text: Which X is silenced is random in each cell. Calico cats prove it—each orange/black patch reflects a different X choice.

climax.text: X-inactivation means every woman is a genetic mosaic. Different cells use different X chromosomes.

punchline.text: Every woman is a mosaic. Each cell chose an X.

quiz.question: Why do calico cats have patchy fur colors?
